column2: Hold the Feast of the Blazing Sun

In high summer the faithful of Myrmidia, the Eagle of the South, honour her with a month of feasting, the Spear Procession under the noon sun and a great service in her temple. Invite your vassals to share it.
Holding the Feast of the Blazing Sun
This character is hosting the Feast of the Blazing Sun in honour of Myrmidia.
The heralds are ready to ride. The Feast of the Blazing Sun will soon begin, and every vassal of mine shall be bidden to come and honour Myrmidia at my side.
Send out the invitations.
Your vassals are invited to the Feast of the Blazing Sun

Greetings, and the blessing of the Eagle upon you.

The summer sun stands high and the Feast of the Blazing Sun is at hand. Come to my court, walk with us in the Spear Procession and hear the hymns in Myrmidia's temple. There will be wine, music and good company.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
I will come.
I must decline.
Your liege is told you will not come

Greetings.

I am sorry, but I cannot attend your feast this summer.

[From.GetTitledFirstName]
Then the Eagle will not see your face either.

The Feast of the Blazing Sun has begun. Golden banners hang from every tower, the tables groan under bread, olives and roasted kid, and the priests of Myrmidia polish the ceremonial spears for the procession. For a month my court belongs to the Eagle of the South.
Glory to Myrmidia!
I have arrived at my liege's court for the Feast of the Blazing Sun. Golden banners hang from every tower and the whole city smells of roasting meat and incense.
The Feast of the Blazing Sun is over. The banners come down, the guests ride home and the priests carry the spears back into the temple for another year. The feast was a great success.
Until next summer.
The Feast of the Blazing Sun is over and it is time to ride home. My liege was a generous host.
The Spear Procession

At noon, when the sun is at its fiercest, the faithful march through the streets behind the priests of Myrmidia, each carrying a spear in the goddess's honour. Bareheaded and without water we walk the long way round the city walls to the temple steps, singing the old battle hymns while the crowds cheer. The heat is terrible, but the Eagle of the South watches over those who march for her.
For the Eagle!
The heat of the procession was too much for my old body. My head pounds and I cannot stop shaking. The priests say the goddess tests the faithful, but I fear she has asked more of me than I can give.
I should have stayed in the shade.
Somewhere on the long march the sun got inside my head. I see golden eagles wheeling above me whenever I close my eyes, and I hear the goddess calling me to war against enemies only I can see.
She is calling. Can't you hear her?
As I stared into the white light above the temple, something stared back. It was not Myrmidia. Whatever it was, it is inside me now, and it laughs when the priests pray.
It is only the heat. Surely.
Marching with my spear beneath the blazing sun, I understood at last. The goddess is no story for soldiers. She is real, she is watching, and she expects me to fight for her.
I am the Eagle's spear.
The march was hard, but I finished it with my head high and my spear steady. I have never felt so strong.
Myrmidia favours the hardy.
On the march an old priest told me the goddess's oldest lesson: the battle is won before the first blow is struck. I have not stopped thinking about it.
Strategy is the goddess's gift.
I wanted to look upon the face of the goddess. I stared into the noon sun until the tears ran and the world went white, and when the priests led me back into the shade, the white did not go away.
I have seen her glory. I need see nothing else.

The feast ends in the temple of Myrmidia. Beneath the great bronze eagle the priests chant the deeds of the goddess, from her birth in Tilea to the day she stood among the defenders of Magritta, and the congregation raises its spears as one.
May the Eagle guard us all.

After the service a knight in burnished armour, a golden sun blazing on his breastplate, kneels before me. He brings greetings from the Grand Master of the Knights of the Blazing Sun. The order has heard of my devotion to Myrmidia, and the Grand Master offers me a lance of the order's knights and men-at-arms to fight under my banner.
The Blazing Sun shall ride with me.
A lance of the Knights of the Blazing Sun joins your army at half the usual upkeep.
Thank the Grand Master, but the order is needed elsewhere.

As [From.GetFirstName] is dragged from the great hall, kicking and cursing, [From.GetSheHe] swears that one day [From.GetSheHe] will come back for vengeance and take by the sword the birthright [From.GetSheHe] believes is [From.GetHerHis].

[From.GetFirstName] is dragged from the great hall screaming and weeping, crying that a life shut away in a temple cloister among peasants is no fate for a [From.GetManWoman] of [From.GetHerHis] blood.

Breaking the news to [From.GetFirstName] is not easy. We fight long and say hard words before [From.GetSheHe] understands that nothing will change my mind and that [From.GetSheHe] must go to the temple cloister.

Breaking the news to [From.GetFirstName] is not easy. [From.GetSheHeCap] sheds a few tears before [From.GetSheHe] understands that nothing will change my mind and that [From.GetSheHe] must go to the cloister of the sisters.

[From.GetFirstName] takes the news calmly. [From.GetSheHeCap] tells me [From.GetSheHe] understands my reasons, and that if I wish [From.GetHerHim] to spend [From.GetHerHis] days in the temple cloister, [From.GetSheHe] will obey.

[From.GetFirstName] takes the news calmly. [From.GetSheHeCap] tells me [From.GetSheHe] understands my reasons, and that if I wish [From.GetHerHim] to spend [From.GetHerHis] days among the sisters of the cloister, [From.GetSheHe] will obey.
And good riddance!
It had to be done...
This was not an easy choice.

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We have read your plea for forgiveness. We are certain you will wish to prove that your repentance is sincere by paying a fitting tithe to the temple.

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
Very well.
I have no gold to waste on priests!

The tithe is paid, and [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has at last lifted my excommunication. The temples of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] open their doors to me again, and the faithful may call me one of their own.

The tithe is paid to [FromFrom.PrimaryTitle.GetName], and [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] has at last lifted my excommunication. In the eyes of the [Root.Religion.GetName] world I am once more the rightful [Root.GetTitle].
A steep price for salvation...

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We have read your plea for forgiveness. We are certain you will wish to prove that your repentance is sincere with a public act of contrition before Us and the faithful.

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
Very well.
I will not crawl before any priest!

For three days I kneel in the mud before the temple of [FromFrom.GetFirstName], ash on my head and a penitent's rope about my neck, while the common folk stare. At last the [FromFrom.GetTitle] comes out, grants me forgiveness and lifts my excommunication. The temples of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] are open to me again.

For three days I kneel in the mud before the hall of [FromFrom.GetFirstName], ash on my head, while the common folk stare. At last the [FromFrom.GetTitle] grants me forgiveness and lifts my excommunication. In the eyes of the [Root.Religion.GetName] world I am once more the rightful [Root.GetTitle].
I have never been so ashamed...

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We have read your plea for forgiveness. We are certain you will wish to prove that your repentance is sincere by giving yourself to [From.Religion.GetHighGodName] and swearing a vow of celibacy.

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
Very well.
What?! Never!
The [FromFrom.GetTitle] has bidden me prove my contrition with a strict vow of celibacy. My loose living, [FromFrom.GetSheHe] says, is what led me from the path of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].
[FromFrom.GetSheHeCap] cannot know what I do at night...
Was it really worth it?

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We have read your plea for forgiveness. We are certain you will wish to prove that your repentance is sincere by giving the life of one of your children to the service of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName].

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
As you wish.
Never!

The [FromFrom.GetTitle] has decided that the price of my sins is the life of my [son_monk_candidate.GetSonDaughter] [son_monk_candidate.GetFirstName]. [son_monk_candidate.GetSheHeCap] will leave [Root.Capital.GetName] to take holy vows and serve in the temple for the rest of [son_monk_candidate.GetHerHis] days.
How could I do this to [son_monk_candidate.GetHerHim]?
[son_monk_candidate.GetSheHeCap] will learn to like it.

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We fear your sins are too great to be washed away by a simple act of contrition. If you care for your soul, you will give up the throne your deeds have stained and give yourself wholly to [From.Religion.GetHighGodName].

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
If this is the price...
Never! This throne is my birthright!
I did not see it coming until it was too late. To wash away my sins I must give up my throne. Stripped of every title, I will live out my days in a temple cloister, far from my friends and kin.
I can only hope my heir does better...

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We have read your plea for forgiveness. We are certain you will wish to prove that your repentance is sincere by repealing the godless edict that strips the temple of its rightful authority in your realm.

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
Very well.
These are my lands and *my* priests!
The price of my absolution is the temple's power over [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. Once again the [FromFrom.GetTitle] alone may name the priests of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] in my own realm.
The price of my absolution is the power of the priesthood over [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName]. Once again the [FromFrom.GetTitle] alone may name the priests in my own realm.
What else could I do?

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We believe it was pride and a selfish hunger for power that led you into sin. In return for absolution, you will show your humility by dividing your realm equally among your heirs.

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
Very well.
Never!

By decree of the temple, my titles will be split equally among my children when I die. The unity of my realm is a steep price for absolution, but I may stand among the faithful of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] once more.

By decree of [FromFrom.PrimaryTitle.GetName], my titles will be split equally among my children when I die. The unity of my realm is a steep price for absolution, but I may stand among my fellow [Root.Religion.GetName] lords once more.
A harsh price indeed...

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We have read your plea for forgiveness. We are certain you will wish to prove that your repentance is sincere by returning to the Lady the holy chapels that are hers by ancient right.

In the name of the Lady of the Lake,
[From.GetTitledName]
Very well.
Those lands are mine now!
With the Lady's chapels returned to [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName], [FromFrom.GetSheHe] has at last absolved me and lifted my excommunication. I may kneel at the Grail shrines in peace again.
A needed sacrifice.

To [Root.GetTitledName],
We have read your plea for forgiveness. We are certain you will wish to prove that your repentance is sincere by recognising that the temple of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName] answers to no mortal lord, yourself included.

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
Very well.
§Y[From.GetTitledFirstName]§! will become §YIndependent§!.
I will not suffer this insolence!

To be absolved I must first admit the authority the temple holds over me. So I have released [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] from my service, and [FromFrom.GetSheHe] now rules [FromFrom.GetHerHis] lands answerable only to [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].

To be absolved I must first admit the authority [FromFrom.PrimaryTitle.GetName] holds over me. So I have released [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName] from my service, and [FromFrom.GetSheHe] now rules [FromFrom.GetHerHis] lands as [FromFrom.GetSheHe] sees fit.
Unfortunate, but necessary.

To [Root.GetTitledName],
Only under the guidance of the temple will you find absolution for your sins. Your lands lie in the shadow of Our own and should rightly answer to [From.Religion.GetHighGodName]. We therefore require you to swear fealty to Us forthwith.

In the name of [From.Religion.GetHighGodName],
[From.GetTitledName]
Very well.
I bow to no priest!
To find absolution I have bent the knee to [FromFrom.GetTitledFirstName]. [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] was free until now, but from this day it answers to the temple of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName].
How humiliating...
Declaration of Repentance
Write to the head of the [Root.Religion.GetName] faith and beg forgiveness for your sins, in the hope that your excommunication will be lifted. A price will be asked.
The head of your faith will consider your plea and name the price of absolution.

That smooth and slightly malty taste, refreshing with just the right amount of bitter. The brothers of the temple brew it to an old recipe they swear was blessed by the god himself, and it is easy to believe. Ah, these monks certainly know the art of brewing!
I must visit the temple more often.
Thanks but no thanks.

Such a wonderful bouquet. The complex blend of flavours spreads over my tongue just as the warmth spreads in my belly. The brothers press it from the temple's own vines on the sunny slopes below their walls. These monks certainly know how to make a fine wine!
[Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s from a nearby temple have arrived bringing healing herbs, poultices and prayers, and offer to help treat my illness.
Thank them and let them help me.
I think not - these herbs smell funny.

One day, passing by a temple, I come upon a [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle] sitting and painting in a field. I watch his work and marvel at the composition, the colours and the fine brush strokes that bring the simple canvas to life: [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] in glory, so real that one could almost hear the god speak. This priest is truly an artistic prodigy.
I will buy this painting and hang it in my hall!
Very nice, now let's eat.

On a courtesy visit to the high [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle] of a local temple, I watch a group of monks copying beautifully illuminated books by candlelight: the deeds of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName], lives of the saints and old chronicles, every page bordered with gold leaf.
I will buy a few books. Perhaps I'll even read them.
Pretty pictures, but I have more important things to do.
[Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]s from the nearby temple have been stopping by to trade for supplies quite often lately. They usually linger to talk and exchange news and learning.
I should seek their company more often.
How tedious, these men of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName].
The high [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle] of a nearby temple has asked that I make a donation towards the repairs of the main shrine. Surely it wouldn't hurt to be named in the priest's rites?
[Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] will know that I support the temple.
Sorry, I can't spare the gold right now.

I woke this morning to blood on my sheets. On the palms of my hands are wounds that will not close - the very wounds [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] is said to have borne. The priests whisper that it is a sign, and my servants make the holy sign whenever I pass.
I am chosen!
What madness is this?

As I lead my troops on campaign, a sergeant rides up and asks to speak to me. He presents a small blackened box, found by a foraging party in the ashes of a temple: inside, wrapped in silk, lies the finger bone of a martyr of [Root.Religion.GetName].
This shall henceforth be an heirloom of my family.
I will give it to the temple back home.

One day at the market, a strange man sidles up and offers to sell me what he swears is the finger bone of a saint of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]. I look at it carefully, and the reliquary at least is very fine.
I must purchase this most sacred relic!
This could be a random piece of junk.

A [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle] of [Root.Religion.GetHighGodName] has arrived and asked for an audience. His small shrine can no longer protect the holy relic it keeps, with robbers and beastmen plaguing the countryside, and he asks my family to keep it safe.
Fear not, we shall protect it.
That old relic that has been in my family's care... I realise I haven't seen it in a very long time. I look for it, but I can't find it anywhere. Why do these things always happen to me?
Better not mention this to anyone.
Enemy raiders have burned the chapel where my family's relic was kept. The [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle] who tended it tried to stop them and was cut down on the doorstep. The relic is gone.
Thieves and murderers!

Disaster, my [Root.GetLordLady]! A stray dog went for the court chaplain while he was carrying the family reliquary, and the relic fell out on the floor. And... well, the dog... we found it burying the bone in the yard among a great many other bones. Now it's impossible to tell which is which.
Curses! My ancestors will be turning in their graves.
Just put any bone in there, no one will know the difference.
Hang on, let me see...
My court chaplain suggests that the family relic might drive out my sickness. A night of prayers in its presence might bring [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]'s eye upon me.
Our holy relic will surely be my salvation!
Bring a healer, and keep that old bone away from me.

As the farmers prepare for the sowing, my court chaplain suggests that we carry the holy relic in procession through the fields to bless them. Surely this would bring a bountiful harvest, and the peasants would love it.
Yes, it will bless the land and please the peasants.
No, I don't think it would do any good.

Holy relics of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName], cheap, boxes of ten!\nA high ranking [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle] tells me that false relics are being sold at the market for great profit: pig knuckles, splinters of firewood, vials of river water. They bring a lot of trade and taxes, but still, it's rather immoral.
Crack down on these criminals!
Leave them be.
Get in on the business!

A local [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle] has petitioned me to give my family's relic to his temple. After all, he says, it isn't right that one family should keep what belongs to all the faithful of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName].
I will give it discreetly.
I will prepare a grand ceremony to hand it over.
Who will rid me of this turbulent [Root.Religion.GetPriestTitle]?
The Skaranorak Temples

I have received a visitor, a monk of the famous Skaranorak Temples of Sigmar in Pfungzig. He tells me that the brothers there spend much of their days in prayer, and that they always name the most pious lords of the Empire in those prayers.\n\nIf I were to show my piety with a large gift of gold to the temples, I would surely be among those the monks remember.
Here, take this gold for the glory of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName].
My piety needs no gold to prove it.
An Invitation to Pfungzig

My [Root.GetLordLady], we have received an invitation to visit the famous Skaranorak Temples of Sigmar in Pfungzig!\n\nIt would make a most interesting journey. The temples have grown to great prominence and power since they were founded on the site of Sigmar's victory over the dragon ogre Skaranorak. Fed by their own farms and by generous gifts, they are a great centre of wealth and learning, second in the Empire only to the Great Temple of Sigmar in Altdorf.
I accept the invitation.
I have no time for this.
At the Skaranorak Temples

So these are the famous Skaranorak Temples! The chapels tower over a busy complex of granaries, scriptoria and barracks. On the fertile farmland around them novices toil to bring in the grain for the temples' coffers, and monks and flagellants come and go in their hundreds. Learning, piety and power hang in the air. This is a place that enjoys the support of the great Electors, not to mention the Grand Theogonist.\n\nI have a few days to spend here, and I mean to make the most of them.
I will learn how the brothers run their farms.
I will spend my days in the scriptorium.
The flagellants' nights look far more lively...
I will pray at the stone where Sigmar stood.
The Order of Fury

I have received a visitor, a warrior priestess of the Order of Fury from its mother house at Durango. She tells me that the Order is always growing, and trains new priestesses at its holy site. But building for the glory of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] takes earthly gold, she explains, and that is why she has come to me.\n\nIf I were to give the Order a large gift, it would surely become known all over the land, and I would be named in the priestesses' prayers for protection.
An Invitation to Durango

My [Root.GetLordLady], we have received an invitation to visit the mother house of the Order of Fury at Durango! The priestesses guard their domain jealously, and such an invitation is surely a sign of my standing among the faithful.\n\nIt is said that on that spot a girl known only as Fury, filled with the might of Myrmidia, stopped a greenskin Waaagh! all by herself. The place was made holy, and the Order was born there. Men are forbidden to enter, but the priestesses make exceptions for pious benefactors.
With the Order of Fury

So this is the mother house of the Order of Fury! As I arrive, a guard of armoured priestesses escorts me through the sacred walls to the guest barracks. At dawn I wake to the clash of spear on shield as the priestesses go through their daily drill and prayers. This is truly a wondrous place!\n\nI have a few days to spend here, and I mean to make the most of them.
I will learn how the Order keeps its house.
I will study with the Order's scholars.
I will pray beside the priestesses.
Relic of a Martyr
The finger bone of a martyr of the faith, yellow with age, in a silver-gilt reliquary set with a crystal window. The faithful kiss the glass when it is carried past.
[FromFrom.GetFirstName], the Damsel of [From.GetName]

My [Root.GetLordLady], there are strange tidings from the province of [From.GetName]. As our country suffers under the strain of war, a young woman has come forward and declared that the [From.Religion.GetRandomGodName] has spoken to her and instructed her to deliver us from the enemies of our land. She wears armor, wields a sword and rides with the soldiers. Her name is [FromFrom.GetFullName] and she is said to be approaching your court at this very moment to offer her services to you as a leader in the war.\n\nSurely, it's an absurd notion that a young peasant woman should take the role of marshal or general of the [Root.GetTitle]'s armies?
Let us receive her and see what she can do for us.
[From.GetFirstName] – the nobles react

My [Root.GetTitle], the lords of the Realm complain. They think it most unfitting and strange that a young maid of low birth is allowed such a prominent position when there are noble lords aplenty who are much more well prepared and competent to lead your armies. Some of them are asking if you are doing this deliberately to insult them.\n\nThere is also the issue of her claiming to be personally sent by [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] - it sounds rather heretical.
Let them moan. I am the [Root.GetTitle].
I agree, but this woman is popular among the common folk.
Very well, we shall put her on trial for heresy.
[From.GetFirstName] and the [Root.GetTitle]

One evening at court, [From.GetFirstName] approaches you and asks to speak with you in private. You agree and the both of you sit down for a talk in your chambers. [From.GetFirstName] speaks to you of her visions of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] and her quest to save the country from the enemy. She speaks with passion, her simple honesty and forceful zeal both coming across as she looks you in the eyes. She declares her fierce loyalty and love for you as the chosen [Root.GetTitle]. You are quite impressed by her passion, intelligence and sincerity.
Thank you for coming to see me, [From.GetFirstName].
My dearest [From.GetFirstName], you are truly sent by [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]!
We both know you are a powerhungry impostor, [From.GetFirstName].
Love, you say? Come sit over here...
The Mission

[FromFrom.GetFirstName] looks at you seriously. 'I hope you have been listening, my [Root.GetLordLady]. The country is hurting and you, its rightful sovereign, is the one to mend it. I shall aid you, this is the mission I have been given by [From.Religion.GetRandomGodName].'
Very good.
Zeal

[FromFrom.GetFirstName] looks at you with tears of joyous fervour in her eyes. 'My [Root.GetLordLady], you are the highest and also the wisest [Root.GetManWoman] in the realm. [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] shall guide you through me, and the people shall be saved. With the sword of righteousness in my hand, guided by your wisdom and the will of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName], we will be victorious!
So it shall be!
Mistrust

[FromFrom.GetFirstName] stands up, a shocked and bewildered expression or her face. 'My [Root.GetLordLady], your accusation wounds me most deeply! I have heard evil things said of me, but did not think I would hear it from you. Still, my loyalty to you comes from [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] and it's stronger than [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName] who has corrupted your faith. I shall always remain your servant, my [Root.GetLordLady]'.\n\nWith these last words, [FromFrom.GetFirstName] kneels before you, tears of sorrow streaming down her face.
Stop this ridiculous charade, woman.
The Lovers

[FromFrom.GetFirstName] quietly sits down next to you and looks into your eyes. As you embrace her and kiss her, she shudders and whispers: By [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName], see how my hands tremble at your touch. Just as I felt this immense joy mixed with bewilderment when [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] first spoke to me, so do I now feel my blood rushing in the same way in your presence. It seems to me that it is the will of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] that we shall be together.'
Come to my bedchamber then, [FromFrom.GetFirstName].
[FromFrom.GetFirstName] the Chaste

[FromFrom.GetFirstName] recoils away from your advances, her eyes expressing surprise, sorrow and anger as she looks at you. By [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName], I did not think the [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodNameCap] would have sown such dark seeds in you as to try and impose on my chastity! I belong to [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] and to none else. Rest assured, my [Root.GetLordLady] - my loyalty to you is untouched, but so shall my body also remain, lest it be the touch of cold steel and martyrdom.'
I see.
[From.GetFirstName] and the common folk

The entire country is boiling with rumours and gossip of [From.GetFullName], the humble country girl who rose to become a trusted servant of the [Root.GetTitle]. Hope of defeating the realm's enemies is blossoming, and peasants everywhere are celebrating this fantastic tale of a virgin saviour from the humblest ranks of society.
She is truly a legend in her own time!
[From.GetFirstName] requests an audience

[From.GetFirstName] has come before you asking to speak to you at the council. She says that the military establishment seems trapped in old doctrines and that the commanders would benefit from more offensive thinking, as well as more religious schooling, of course.\n\nThere is grumbling from some of the assembled nobles at her speech.
Thank you, [From.GetFirstName], that's a good idea.
When I need your advice, I'll ask for it.
I've had enough of this insolence – arrest her!
[From.GetFirstName] and the temples

Your [Root.GetLordSpiritualName] [Root.job_spiritual.GetFullName] approaches you one morning for a candid conversation: 'My [Root.GetLordLady], there is much displeasure among the clergy at the elevation of this young woman, [From.GetFirstName]. The things she says are considered heretical by some, and others, frankly, see their positions threatened by one of such low birth and meager schooling gaining so much prestige. I would advise you to consider whether it is worth protecting this young lass at so great a potential cost.'
Please remind these clergymen who is [Root.GetTitle].
She is merely a tool, the temples have nothing to fear.
Very well, we will put her on trial and see if she is a heretic.
The influence of [From.GetFirstName]

These are unusual times. [From.GetFirstName]'s influence is felt all around, wherever you go. There is a surge in religiosity among the commoners, who see her as a national saviour and almost a divine-figure. Among the nobles many are charmed by her pious innocence and energetic zeal, in spite of most of them also viewing her as a dangerous upstart. Meanwhile, the clergy is divided, some seeing a heretic and others a saint.
We should all try to be more like her.
I dislike fanatics, but I will suffer her for now.
A common girl from [From.GetName]

Your [Root.GetChancellorName] [Root.job_chancellor.GetFullName] comes to see you, a look of worry on [Root.job_chancellor.GetHerHis] face. [Root.job_chancellor.GetSheHe] explains that there are increased grumblings among the nobles regarding the position of your protegé [FromFrom.GetFirstName]. Many of them refuse to accept that a lowborn woman from [From.GetName], however competent and pious, be continuously given so many privileges normally reserved for nobility. It sets a bad example for the peasants and may cause unrest, they fear. There have also been numerous incidents of perceived insults and scandals of protocol between [FromFrom.GetFirstName] and various prestigious army commanders.\n\nIt seems many nobles feel they have suffered her too long, and some still entertain the idea of demanding her arrest and trial for heresy.
Bah! Their own incompetence makes them envious.
I shall force her to speak more humbly henceforth.
Not noble enough? Bring her before me and I shall knight her!
I cannot abide this any longer. Put her in chains!
[From.GetFirstName] marries

Never has the realm seen so much attention focused on the wedding of one who is not of noble birth. The wedding of [From.GetFirstName] has caused ringing of temple bells and impromptu feasts and prayers among the common folk all around the country.\n\nNo longer a maid perhaps, but an icon of the realm still, and even the [Root.GetTitle] should make sure to make a public toast to the newly-weds.
Indeed!
[From.GetFirstName] the mother

[From.GetFirstName] the Damsel she used to be, but no longer. Some of her followers speak of a virgin birth, though such talk is frowned upon by the clergy. The image of [From.GetFirstName] has now changed in the eyes of many, but she continues to be a focus of adulation, and very soon after the birth she has once again taken up her sword and saddled her horse.
So strong!
The trial of [From.GetFirstName]

[From.GetFirstName] has been put on trial for heresy. She claims to be sent by [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName], to be a messenger. She is accused of being sent by the [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodName], and of claiming to be [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName]'s chosen one, and of knowingly promoting religious confusion, among other things. The judges come mostly from the clergy, and they begin a hard line of questioning against the young woman. There is unrest outside the castle where the trial is held, as many followers have come to pray for her and express their belief in her innocence. This trial seems set to last for a while.
The truth shall be our only concern.
The trial of [FromFrom.GetFirstName] – judgement

[FromFrom.GetFirstName] has been put through long sessions of questioning for over a month now. After much deliberation on the law and theology and evaluation of testimony the case still seems unclear to many. It all seems to come down to whether you want to believe that she is a messenger of [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] or of the [Root.Religion.GetRandomEvilGodNameCap]. Or perhaps it's more down to whether it is politically expedient to convict her or not. Young [FromFrom.GetFirstName] herself has assumed a position of sorrowful fatalism. She says she has seen her fate in a vision and that she knows what is to come.\nThe crowds surrounding the trial all await the verdict with tension. If [FromFrom.GetFirstName] were to be acquitted, the humiliation of the trial itself surely signifies that she has fallen from royal grace and will never come back to hold the position she once did. But in the case of a conviction, a gruesome death by burning at the stake is certain to be the fate that awaits her. There is little mercy for heretics.
She is guilty.
She is innocent.
The execution of [From.GetFirstName]

The flames leap higher and higher, crackling as they begin to eat at the wood. Slowly, [From.GetFirstName] starts to twist as they begin to lick her legs. The gathered crowd stares in stunned silence - some hungry for her death, others overcome by horror at what they see. The life of this woman is coming to an end, she who captured the attention of the entire realm during these months. Saint or heretic – the eyes of the onlookers hold different views, but it seems certain that she will remembered for many many years. Perhaps she shall have her restitution in time, perhaps not.\nAs the flames climb higher and take hold of [From.GetFirstName]'s body, she twitches violently but still does not cry out. Her gaze is fixed on the heavens, tears streaming from her face. Many onlookers turn away now, but others are fixed to the spot, unable to avert their eyes. Slowly, [From.GetFirstName] disappears from view as the flames rise around her.
May [Root.Religion.GetRandomGodName] have mercy on her soul.
[From.GetFirstName] is aquitted

The acquittal of [From.GetFirstName] have left mixed reactions across the realm. There are celebrations among the peasants, and more mixed reactions among the nobility and clergy. [From.GetFirstName] herself spends these days in prayer. She realizes that she may not lead armies again nor enjoy the ear of the [Root.GetTitle] as before. Still, the acquittal at the trial has vindicated her words and actions and she seems at peace. No longer on the grand stage of war and politics, she seems now content to spend the rest of her days living as a nun.
You are safe now, [From.GetFirstName].
Years later...

After the first turbulent years, it seems everyone in the country has gotten used to [FromFrom.GetFullName]. Some appreciate her and some do not, but the more violent controversy and commotion has died out and people are now preoccupied with other matters. She lives on, although the tales of the early years of the Hero of [From.GetName] are already the stuff of legend.
So be it.
If you are lucky, [From.GetFirstName] may become your lover.

Rejoice, children of Myrmidia! After the miraculous recovery of territory lost centuries ago, Myrmidia's Empire has been reborn! Tilea and Estalia have endured dark times. After the era of Myrmidia Incarnate, our lands were stormed by Greenskins, bandits, pretenders and northern barbarians, and territory after territory burned at their touch, but now a bright new age has dawned for all of civilization.\n\n[Root.GetTitledFirstName] has been crowned by the Última Águila as Myrmidia Incarnate at the great cathedral of Magritta, and now rules [Root.PrimaryTitle.GetName] as the second Incarnation of Myrmidia!
Myrmidia's Empire
Myrmidia Invicta!
